co-2901.title: Pavement: reddish tiles
co-2901.summary: Sidewalks are often decorated with reddish tiles.

co-44Li.title: Landscape: extreme dry, low plants, cacti
co-44Li.summary: Typical of La Guajira in the far north: extreme dryness, low vegetation and occasional cacti. The straight Uribia to Puerto Bolívar road has a railway always on its east side.

co-45F4.title: Kilometre marker: tall green 'Pr' or stone
co-45F4.summary: Two types, both unique: a tall green marker with the letters Pr at the top, and a traditional stone one with black lettering. The first two digits at the bottom are the road number and the last two are the road section.

co-4oTi.title: Road: narrow strip between sea and shallow water
co-4oTi.summary: The narrow Ruta 90 strip between Barranquilla and Ciénaga has dashed yellow lines, shallow water beside it and open sea often to the north. Older Gen 3 also shows tall mountains in the distance.

co-5AfA.title: Google car: unique vehicle, long concrete blocks
co-5AfA.summary: A unique vehicle around Leticia, the southernmost town. Long concrete blocks at the bottom left reliably mark the road north of it.

co-A1PS.title: Landscape: white sandy soil, dry
co-A1PS.summary: The north has white, sandy soil and a dry, arid landscape.

co-AbNO.title: Google car: small white truck, no antenna
co-AbNO.summary: On San Andrés island the coverage was taken by a small white truck with no antenna.

co-AsK1.title: Plants: sugar cane fields along a river
co-AsK1.summary: Sugar cane is grown along the Cauca river in Valle del Cauca and neighbouring departments.

co-D97d.title: People: mostly Afro-Colombian on Pacific coast
co-D97d.summary: Because of the slave trade, the Pacific coast has an overwhelming majority of Afro-Colombians.

co-FhGC.title: Google car: small grey-silver truck, long antenna
co-FhGC.summary: On Providencia island, about 90 km north of San Andrés, Google used a small grey or silver truck with a long antenna.

co-JMPO.title: Direction sign: white metal posts, cross at back
co-JMPO.summary: Signposts are white metal and join to form a distinct cross on the back of the sign. Brazil has white metal posts too, but they are usually wider.

differs.how: Brazilian white metal posts are usually wider

co-OUrh.title: Pole: concrete, often dark, sometimes octagonal
co-OUrh.summary: Poles are mostly concrete with many kinds of tops, and dark-coloured poles are more common here than next door. Octagonal poles in the Americas are only in Colombia, Mexico and Ecuador.

co-PQZi.title: Lamp post: green with trapezoid metal support
co-PQZi.summary: Green street lights held up by a trapezoidal metal sheet underneath. The same odd-shaped support is also found in Barranquilla.

co-ay1W.title: Plate: yellow
co-ay1W.summary: Colombian plates are typically yellow. In South America yellow plates are almost only found here.

co-cSUD.title: Pole: black-yellow or black-orange stripes
co-cSUD.summary: Poles are often marked with black-and-yellow or black-and-orange stripes.

co-fexW.title: Pole paint: black ends, long yellow middle
co-fexW.summary: A short black strip at top and bottom with a longer yellow section between. Most common in Antioquia, sometimes in Córdoba.

co-kWTr.title: Street marker: small concrete post with names
co-kWTr.summary: In Barranquilla, intersections are marked by small concrete posts (mojones) showing the street names.

co-lm-2884.title: Landscape: dry coast with many cacti
co-lm-2884.summary: The northern tip looks a lot like the dry coast of northern Peru, but with more cacti and a different Google car.

differs.how: Peru has fewer cacti and a different car

co-lm-298305.title: Landscape: treeless alpine, giant rosette plants
co-lm-298305.summary: Páramo is alpine tundra in the mountains with very little vegetation. The best clue is the odd giant rosette plants. Most common south of Bogotá, still in the capital district.

co-lm-298306.title: Lamp: red lamp style
co-lm-298306.summary: A red lamp style unique to Tolima, only seen in Ibagué. The clue is its colour and shape, not the arrangement of lights.

co-lm-298307.title: Road: orange dust
co-lm-298307.summary: The only road in Guaviare runs south from the city up to Vda. El Trueno and has orange-looking dust on it.

co-lm-298308.title: Bollard: Spanish-style
co-lm-298308.summary: A Spanish-style bollard found in Cundinamarca and on Road 40 towards Villavicencio.

co-lm-298310.title: Bollard: with road names at intersections
co-lm-298310.summary: In Barranquilla you often find this bollard with road names on it at intersections.

co-lm-301790.title: Pole paint: orange and blue
co-lm-301790.summary: Orange and blue pole paint is found in Caldas.

co-lm-301791.title: Soil: deep grey and stony
co-lm-301791.summary: Deep grey, stony soil in Gen 3 coverage, found in towns near the Pacific coast.

co-lm-472824.title: Pole marking: yellow numbers on blue
co-lm-472824.summary: Yellow numbers on a blue background are unique to Valle del Cauca.

co-lm-472825.title: Pole marking: blue numbers on yellow
co-lm-472825.summary: Blue numbers only on a yellow background are unique to Cauca.

co-lm-472826.title: Pole marking: blue numbers with TA or SA, yellow
co-lm-472826.summary: Blue numbers mixed with the letters TA or SA on yellow are unique to Nariño. The next department has blue numbers on yellow without letters.

co-lm-472827.title: Pole marking: orange, blue numbers with a letter
co-lm-472827.summary: In Risaralda and Caldas, orange background with blue numbers that start with a letter. Huila's look very similar, but the numbers are black.

co-lm-472829.title: Plate: blue horizontal plate starting AP
co-lm-472829.summary: A blue horizontal plate starting with AP followed by a few numbers is only found in Cundinamarca.

co-lm-472830.title: Pole marking: white paint, orange numbers
co-lm-472830.summary: In Bogotá and Cundinamarca, poles have white paint with orange vertical numbers.

co-lm-472833.title: Pole marking: orange with black numbers
co-lm-472833.summary: Huila has an orange background with black numbers that start with a letter.

co-lm-472834.title: Pole marking: white vertical numbers on black
co-lm-472834.summary: In Cali and nearby towns, white vertical numbers on a black background.

co-lm-472835.title: Pole marking: white numbers on orange sticker
co-lm-472835.summary: White vertical numbers on an orange plastic sticker are unique to Tolima.

co-lm-472842.title: Pole sticker: orange QR code
co-lm-472842.summary: Orange plastic stickers with a QR code are in Barranquilla and Santa Marta.

co-lm-473889.title: Pole paint: light and dark blue
co-lm-473889.summary: Light and dark blue pole paint is found in Santa Marta.

co-lm-55224.title: Pavement: unique cobblestones
co-lm-55224.summary: A unique cobblestone pavement in the historic town of Barichara, in Santander.

co-lm-55225.title: Road: swampy stretches
co-lm-55225.summary: Roads 74, 78 and a few others further north have very swampy parts. Zoom the map to see where.

co-lm-55226.title: Road: swamp road in very sunny coverage
co-lm-55226.summary: A swamp road with extremely sunny coverage is probably Road 74 in Sucre.

co-lm-55228.title: Road: low clouds, tall mountain to the east
co-lm-55228.summary: Road 78 west of Pailitas has low clouds and a towering mountain on the east side.

co-lm-55229.title: Coverage: Gen 4 grey car, patterns on the map
co-lm-55229.summary: Gen 4 with the grey car is absent north of Montería, has a gap between Bucaramanga and Bogotá, forms a staircase of right angles at Medellín and Bogotá, covers areas around Bucaramanga, and has a missing section around Popayán.

co-lm-55230.title: Coverage: Gen 4 white car, patterns on the map
co-lm-55230.summary: Gen 4 with the white car has no coverage south of Cali, very little around Medellín, and forms a curved pattern around Medellín.

co-lm-55231.title: Coverage: Gen 3 striped car in a straight line
co-lm-55231.summary: Gen 3 with the white-and-blue car follows a straight line between Cartagena and Medellín, with partial coverage along Route 80 west of Bosconia, and along Route 45 north of Bucaramanga and east of Medellín.

co-lm-55232.title: Pole paint: yellow with dark numbers
co-lm-55232.summary: Yellow pole paint with dark numbers, found in Cauca and Nariño.

co-lm-55235.title: Pole paint: yellow with black numbers in rows
co-lm-55235.summary: Yellow paint with black numbers, with several digits in one row. Found in Valle del Cauca.

co-lm-55236.title: Pole paint: green with yellow numbers
co-lm-55236.summary: Green pole paint with yellow numbers, found in coastal Antioquia.

co-lm-55237.title: Pole paint: yellow with red numbers
co-lm-55237.summary: Yellow paint with red numbers. Found all over Risaralda and in the towns of Istmina and Quibdó in Chocó.

co-lm-55239.title: Lamp: H-shaped attachment plate
co-lm-55239.summary: Lamp attachment plates shaped like an H are found in Bogotá.

co-lm-55240.title: Lamp: rectangular attachment plate
co-lm-55240.summary: Rectangular lamp attachment plates are mainly in Medellín, sometimes further north, especially Montería and Cúcuta.

co-lm-55241.title: Plants: tall wax palm
co-lm-55241.summary: The wax palm grows in mountain regions, mainly in Quindío, as the name says.

co-lm-55242.title: Plants: guadua bamboo plantations
co-lm-55242.summary: Guadua bamboo plantations are found mainly in Caldas, but also in neighbouring Tolima, Quindío and Risaralda.

co-lm-55243.title: Plants: oil palm plantations
co-lm-55243.summary: Oil palms are mainly in Meta and Casanare, very common around Route 45 near Fundación and Aracataca, and sometimes around Barrancabermeja.

co-lm-55244.title: Plants: palms with the crown cut off
co-lm-55244.summary: Palms whose crown has been cut are very often found near Aracataca and a few smaller towns north of it.

co-lm-55245.title: Coverage: large lake, mostly winter
co-lm-55245.summary: A large lake (Embalse Calima), mostly with winter coverage and a small stretch of summer coverage.

co-lm-55246.title: Google car: stick on the camera
co-lm-55246.summary: A stick attached to the camera is visible between El Guío and El Boral, near the Cundinamarca-Meta border close to Villavicencio.

co-lm-55247.title: Bus: green or yellow modern bus on own lane
co-lm-55247.summary: Modern green or yellow buses, often on a dedicated lane, are found in the Pereira area.

co-lm-55248.title: Plants: Colombian mahogany tree
co-lm-55248.summary: This tree is found mainly around Medellín, but has been seen in other random places.

co-lm-55249.title: Bus: white Transmetro bus
co-lm-55249.summary: White Transmetro buses are found in Barranquilla.

co-lm-55250.title: Road: bike lane with eastern-lowland feel
co-lm-55250.summary: If you see a bike lane and the land feels like east of the Andes, you're most likely on the road through Los Tobitos to Villavicencio.

co-lm-55251.title: Pavement: plus-shaped stones and puddles
co-lm-55251.summary: Many puddles and pavement made of plus-shaped stones means Tumaco.

co-lm-55252.title: Road: many trucks
co-lm-55252.summary: The stretch of Road 40 to Buenaventura is an important truck route, so lots of trucks is a clue.

co-lm-55253.hide: no learnable content (image-only note about spikes)

co-lm-55254.title: Coverage: rainy, very orange-brown soil
co-lm-55254.summary: Rainy coverage with very orange-brown soil on the road to La Florida.

co-lm-55255.title: Coverage: grey car with 2023 copyright
co-lm-55255.summary: A grey car with 2023 copyright appears on Road 65 in Caquetá and Road 45 in Putumayo.

co-lm-55256.title: Coverage: lake with overexposed Gen 4
co-lm-55256.summary: A lake together with overexposed Gen 4 camera probably means the lake south of Sogamoso.

co-lm-55258.title: Google car: second Google car visible
co-lm-55258.summary: A second Google car shows up in many random spots. Most prominent: Road 26 in Cauca, Vda. Chontaduro near Popayán, and the road between Pital and Tarqui.

co-lm-55259.title: Houses: straw or thatched roofs
co-lm-55259.summary: Houses with roofs like these are common along the coast, especially near Cartagena and Barranquilla.

co-lm-55260.title: Houses: bright colours, unique pavement
co-lm-55260.summary: Brightly coloured houses and a unique pavement mark the town of Guatapé.

co-lm-55261.title: Bus: red Tinto bus
co-lm-55261.summary: A red bus that only drives in the town of Armenia.

co-lm-55262.title: Coverage: trekker with unique pavement, houses
co-lm-55262.summary: The Trebal Resort trekker can be recognised by its unique pavement and houses.

co-lm-55263.title: Vans: TransLago minivans
co-lm-55263.summary: TransLago vans are common across Boyacá, most often on the Tunja to Sogamoso and Tunja to Duitama routes.

co-lm-55264.title: Coverage: rain with heavy fog
co-lm-55264.summary: Rainy coverage combined with strong fog means Road 64.

co-lm-55265.title: Coverage: rainy
co-lm-55265.summary: Rainy coverage is most common on highways 20, 24, 50 and 64.

co-lm-55266.title: Road: flat, sunset through clouds, mountains NW
co-lm-55266.summary: On the road from Tame to Hato Corozal you see a slight sunset through the clouds. It is quite flat with mountains to the northwest.

co-lm-55267.title: Road: sunset through the clouds
co-lm-55267.summary: On the road from Tame to Arauca you can see a sunset through the clouds, though it is not always easy to recognise.

co-lm-55268.title: Google car: second car on a side road
co-lm-55268.summary: A second Google car can be seen on Carrera 4, a side road off Route 45 near Aguachica.

co-lm-55269.title: Google car: second car on east-west road
co-lm-55269.summary: A second Google car can be seen on the east-west road just south of the Guayuriba River, south of Villavicencio.

co-lm-55270.title: Landscape: hazy Gen 4 with red dirt
co-lm-55270.summary: The Vichada area has hazy Gen 4 coverage and red dirt.

co-lm-55271.title: Landscape: red-orange dirt in an urban Gen 4 spot
co-lm-55271.summary: Santa Rosalía is the only town covered in Vichada, so red or orange dirt in an urban Gen 4 location points there.

co-lm-55272.title: Plants: common guava trees
co-lm-55272.summary: Guava mostly grows in the valley between the western and central mountain ranges, but can appear in other valleys too.

co-lm-55273.title: Plants: coffee belt
co-lm-55273.summary: The coffee belt runs through the valley between Medellín and Cali. In the north it is only near the Venezuelan border. Olives and tea have a similar spread.

co-lm-55274.title: Plants: wide trees near fences
co-lm-55274.summary: Wide trees, usually near fences, grow in northern regions, especially around Montería and Sincelejo.

co-lm-55275.title: Plants: cacti
co-lm-55275.summary: Cacti are most common in the north near Valledupar and sometimes appear in Huila.

co-lm-55276.title: Plants: kapok tree
co-lm-55276.summary: The kapok tree occurs throughout the country but is most common between the central and eastern mountain ranges.

co-lm-717431.title: Coverage: always cloudy, small camera rift
co-lm-717431.summary: On the road in Arauca and in Arauca city, in the northeast, almost all coverage is cloudy and bad weather. A small camera glitch shows a rift northeast of the driving direction.

co-lm-717460.title: Landscape: hilly fields with thick hedges
co-lm-717460.summary: In the south around Pasto, hilly fields are bordered by thick hedges that form lines on the hills, with a British feel. Very rarely seen elsewhere in Colombia. Ecuador has such fields too, so be sure you are in Colombia.

differs.how: Ecuador also has hedged hilly fields

co-lm-717461.title: Plants: banana plantations behind hedges
co-lm-717461.summary: In Quindío, banana plantations are commonly behind hedges.

co-lm-717462.title: Plants: small banana fields, no hedge
co-lm-717462.summary: In the states around Quindío, smaller banana plantations lie along the road without hedges.

co-lm-717463.title: Plants: banana plantations in cloudy Gen 3
co-lm-717463.summary: Large banana plantations appear in several areas. With cloudy Gen 3 coverage they are most common in northwest Antioquia.

co-lm-717464.title: Plants: bananas on dry sandy ground
co-lm-717464.summary: In Magdalena, banana plantations often sit on dry, sandy or dirty ground with mountains to the east.

co-lm-717465.title: Plants: tree with a knot atop its trunk
co-lm-717465.summary: Trees that look like they have a knot on top of the trunk grow most in dark red areas. Córdoba has the most Gen 4, so seeing them in Gen 4 suggests Córdoba. They also appear in mountains.

co-lm-717466.title: Pole top: Valle del Cauca style
co-lm-717466.summary: These particular pole tops mean you are in Valle del Cauca.

co-lm-717467.title: Landscape: cone-shaped mountain
co-lm-717467.summary: A striking cone-shaped mountain, often visible from around Guatapé.

co-lm-717468.title: Electricity meter: tall box with oval windows
co-lm-717468.summary: Tall meter boxes with oval windows. Round windows are less reliable. Very common here because there are few plastic meters.

co-lm-717469.title: Pole: lopsided with a vertical stalk on top
co-lm-717469.summary: Asymmetrical poles with a vertical stalk coming out of the top are often found east of the Andes, though not always.

co-lm-717470.title: Plants: banana plantations
co-lm-717470.summary: Banana plantations are mainly in Quindío and Magdalena, sometimes in northwest Antioquia and Córdoba, and rarely in provinces around Quindío.

co-mZY9.title: Landscape: huge lowland, savanna, seasonal floods
co-mZY9.summary: East of the Andes is a vast lowland of open grassland and savannah with scattered trees, small forests and seasonal flooding. You may see mountains to the west, but never to the east.

co-oKQt.title: Coverage: mostly north and west, plus islands
co-oKQt.summary: Coverage is mainly in the north and west. The islands of Providencia and San Andrés, northwest of the mainland, are covered too.

co-qLYa.title: Coverage: oversaturated patch in the image
co-qLYa.summary: A camera glitch makes part of the image look very saturated, found in southern Colombia.

co-rkhV.title: Google car: short thick antenna on black car
co-rkhV.summary: In Gen 3 a short thick antenna is sometimes visible on a black, white or grey car; in Gen 4 the car is commonly white or silver. Mexico, Ecuador and Brazil have the antenna too, but only here is it on a black car.

co-uYGd.title: Fence: wooden posts, some painted and pointed
co-uYGd.summary: Wooden fences are very common. Some posts are painted and sharp at the top, which is almost exclusive to Colombia.

co-wre8.title: Taxi: pastel yellow, white plate
co-wre8.summary: Taxis are always pastel yellow, with white plates often printed on the side and roof, and the city name if unblurred. Ecuadorian taxis are a slightly more saturated yellow with orange plates.

differs.how: Ecuadorian taxis are more saturated yellow with orange plates
